question: According to the SC CDL manual, which trailer in a doubles or triples combination is most likely to turn over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
choice_a: The last trailer in the combination
choice_b: The first trailer (closest to the tractor)
choice_c: The tractor itself
choice_d: The converter dolly
explanation: The manual states that because of the crack-the-whip effect, the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over, so drivers must steer gently.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.2, Beware of the Crack-the-whip Effect

question: The manual warns that a safe speed on a curve for a straight truck or a single trailer combination vehicle may be:
choice_a: Exactly the same for doubles and triples
choice_b: Too fast for a set of doubles or triples
choice_c: Too slow for doubles or triples
choice_d: Irrelevant to doubles and triples
explanation: The manual specifically notes that a safe curve speed for a straight truck or single trailer may be too fast for a set of doubles or triples, so drivers must steer gently and go slowly.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.1, Prevent Trailer from Rolling Over

topic: Antilock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies
question: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes and will have what indicator?
choice_a: A red lamp on the right side of the dolly
choice_b: A green lamp on the rear of the dolly
choice_c: A yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly
choice_d: No visible indicator is required
explanation: The manual states that converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 must have antilock brakes and will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.8, Antilock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

question: When parking a doubles or triples combination, the manual advises drivers to:
choice_a: Always back into the space to save time
choice_b: Disconnect the rear trailer before parking
choice_c: Park only in spaces marked for single trailers
choice_d: Avoid a spot you cannot pull straight through
explanation: The manual states you should be aware of how parking lots are arranged and avoid a spot you cannot pull straight through, to avoid a long and difficult escape.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.7, Parking the Vehicle

question: For the safest handling on the road when coupling twin trailers, where should the more heavily loaded semitrailer be positioned?
choice_a: In the first position behind the tractor
choice_b: In the second (rear) position
choice_c: On the converter dolly
choice_d: It does not matter as long as both are secured
explanation: The manual states that for the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers

question: If the second (rear) trailer does not have spring brakes, how do you set its emergency brakes before coupling?
choice_a: Apply the trolley valve repeatedly
choice_b: Drive the tractor close, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line
choice_c: Chock the wheels only; brakes cannot be set this way
choice_d: Push the tractor protection valve control in
explanation: The manual explains that if the second trailer lacks spring brakes, you drive close, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line to set the trailer emergency brakes, chocking wheels if in doubt.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers, Secure Second (Rear) Trailer

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, the trailer height must be:
choice_a: Exactly level with the fifth wheel
choice_b: Higher than the center of the fifth wheel
choice_c: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel
choice_d: Adjusted only after coupling is complete
explanation: The manual states the trailer must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When making a visual check of the coupling between the converter dolly and the rear trailer, what should you confirm?
choice_a: The parking brake light is illuminated
choice_b: The landing gear is fully lowered
choice_c: The tractor protection valve has popped out
choice_d: No space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to make a visual check of the coupling, confirming there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, how do you test that the coupling is secure?
choice_a: Pull against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_b: Apply the trailer service brakes
choice_c: Check the tire pressure
choice_d: Sound the horn while pulling forward
explanation: The manual lists testing the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer as one of the required coupling steps.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It will drain the air brake system
choice_b: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury
choice_c: It voids the manufacturer's warranty
choice_d: It will trigger the antilock brake warning lamp
explanation: The manual explicitly warns to never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling difficult.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.2, Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: What is the first step listed for uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles?
choice_a: Release the dolly brakes
choice_b: Disconnect all dolly air and electric lines
choice_c: Park the rig in a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_d: Lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer
explanation: The uncoupling procedure begins with parking the rig in a straight line on firm level ground before applying parking brakes and proceeding with the remaining steps.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.2, Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is uncoupled first?
choice_a: The trailer closest to the tractor (first trailer)
choice_b: All three trailers are uncoupled simultaneously
choice_c: The second trailer
choice_d: The third (rearmost) trailer, by pulling the dolly out
explanation: The manual states you first uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitch the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, before uncoupling the remainder of the rig.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.3, Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: For coupling and uncoupling combinations other than the common tractor-trailer types, the manual instructs drivers to:
choice_a: Learn the correct method according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications
choice_b: Use the twin trailer method for all combinations
choice_c: Contact SCDMV before every trip
choice_d: Only use combinations built after 1998
explanation: The manual notes there are too many combination types to cover and directs drivers to learn the correct coupling/uncoupling method according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.4, Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: To inspect a doubles or triples combination vehicle, the manual directs drivers to use:
choice_a: A simplified three-step check
choice_b: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_c: Only a visual walk-around with no hands-on checks
choice_d: The single-vehicle inspection checklist, unmodified
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect a combination vehicle, plus additional checks specific to doubles and triples.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.3, Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel during inspection, the locking jaws should be around:
choice_a: The head of the kingpin
choice_b: The release arm only
choice_c: The shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_d: The glide plate
explanation: The additional checks for the coupling system specify that the locking jaws should be around the shank of the kingpin, not the head.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.3.1, Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When checking a sliding fifth wheel, you should confirm it is not so far forward that:
choice_a: The trailer brakes will fail
choice_b: The dolly will separate from the trailer
choice_c: The kingpin will disengage from the fifth wheel
choice_d: The tractor frame will hit the landing gear or the cab will hit the trailer during turns
explanation: The manual warns to check that the fifth wheel is not so far forward that the tractor frame will hit the landing gear, or the cab will hit the trailer, during turns.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.3.1, Additional Checks, Sliding Fifth Wheel

question: For the shut-off valves at the rear of doubles and triples trailers, what should the position be at the rear of the front trailers versus the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Rear of front trailers: OPEN; rear of last trailer: CLOSED
choice_b: All shut-off valves should be CLOSED
choice_c: Rear of front trailers: CLOSED; rear of last trailer: OPEN
choice_d: All shut-off valves should be OPEN
explanation: The manual specifies that the shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.3.1, Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: During inspection of a doubles or triples rig, the converter dolly air tank drain valve should be:
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: CLOSED
choice_c: Set to "emergency"
choice_d: Removed for cleaning
explanation: The manual lists the converter dolly air tank drain valve as an item that should be CLOSED during inspection.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.3.2, Additional Things to Check during a Walk-around Inspection

question: When testing the tractor protection valve, it should pop out (or move to the "emergency" position) when air pressure falls into a range usually specified as:
choice_a: 5 to 10 psi
choice_b: 60 to 90 psi
choice_c: 20 to 45 psi
choice_d: 100 to 120 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) usually pops out when air pressure falls within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: To check that air flows to all trailers, you go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer. What should you hear if the system is properly charged?
choice_a: Silence, indicating no leaks
choice_b: A clicking sound from the tractor protection valve
choice_c: The parking brake release chime
choice_d: Air escaping, showing the entire system is charged
explanation: The manual states that when you open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer, you should hear air escaping, which shows the entire system is charged.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: To test the trailer emergency brakes, after charging the system you pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in "emergency") and then:
choice_a: Pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the emergency brakes are on
choice_b: Immediately release the tractor parking brake
choice_c: Disconnect the electrical cord and observe the lights
choice_d: Check the tire tread depth
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to pull gently on the trailer with the tractor after placing the trailer air supply control in the emergency position, to confirm the trailer emergency brakes are on.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Emergency Brakes

question: The manual states trailer service brakes should be tested using which control, even though normal operation uses the foot pedal?
choice_a: The parking brake lever
choice_b: The hand control (trolley valve)
choice_c: The tractor protection valve
choice_d: The converter dolly release arm
explanation: The manual explains that trailer brakes should be tested with the hand valve (trolley valve), even though in normal operation they are controlled with the foot pedal.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Service Brakes

question: Why does the manual instruct drivers of doubles/triples to look far ahead down the road?
choice_a: To spot weigh stations in advance
choice_b: To find the nearest parking area
choice_c: So you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary, avoiding rollover or jackknife
choice_d: To read overhead signage sooner
explanation: The manual states doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife, so drivers should look far ahead in order to slow down or change lanes gradually.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.4, Look Far Ahead

question: Why does the manual emphasize inspecting "completely" for doubles and triples specifically?
choice_a: Because fewer parts need checking than on a single vehicle
choice_b: Because inspections are only required annually
choice_c: Because doubles and triples are exempt from Section 2 inspection
choice_d: Because there are more critical parts to check when you have two or three trailers
explanation: The manual states there are more critical parts to check when you have two or three trailers, so you must check them all following the procedures described in the section.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.1.3, Inspect Completely

question: According to the manual, a converter dolly is best described as:
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_b: A braking device installed only on the tractor
choice_c: A type of parking brake control
choice_d: An electronic stability control system
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer
